summary: Evening burst caused reserved-pool GPU starvation and noisy-tenant slot contention for dedicated customer
description: Issue summary: LexaAI reports severe throughput degradation on their dedicated reserved pool during an evening traffic spike (approx 18:10-18:40 UTC). Symptoms included long queue growth, repeated request retries from their SDK, and elevated p99 latency. Impact: customer-facing inference degraded by ~65% at p50 and p99 latency jumped from 120ms to 1.8s for short streaming requests. Root-cause not yet confirmed; initial signals point to a combination of slot fragmentation, aggressive micro-bursting by a co-located tenant, and autoscaler not reclaiming cold slots quickly enough. Environment: Dedicated pool (reserved) for LexaAI in us-east, GPU family: A100-80GB heterogeneous cluster, autoscaler version v3.4.2.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer sent a short-streaming workload that includes many concurrent 1-2s inference streams beginning at 18:09 UTC.
2) Observe dedicated pool slot allocation in the us-east cluster over the next 30 minutes.
3) Watch autoscaler metrics for scale-up/scale-down events and pending allocation queue length.
4) Replay similar load on staging with many small concurrent streams to test fragmentation and tail latency.
logs_and_metrics: B) Observed: GPU allocation failures spike (allocation_error_rate went from 0.2% to 12.6% at 18:12 UTC).
C) Autoscaler logs (allocator-003): repeated 'no-fit' decisions due to fragmented free-slot set; sample log 18:14:11 'no-fit for 16-slot request; free contiguous slots insufficient',
D) Request traces: increased retry count from customer SDK and several 503/504 transient errors between 18:11-18:21 UTC.
E) SRE metric: KV cache memory growth on a different tenant (tenant-id: t-3487) correlated with slot hogging and eviction churn.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-12 18:25 - Support triaged with customer, collected SDK logs and trace IDs. Customer confirms spike came from a promotion push causing large number of short streams.

2026-03-12 18:40 - SRE inspected allocator logs: saw repeated placement failures and many small-stream allocations pinned to single GPUs, creating fragmentation and preventing coalescing for larger batched requests.

2026-03-12 19:05 - Hypothesis A: Noisy tenant t-3487 produced many tiny short-lived streams that occupied fractional slots and triggered evictions; autoscaler did not downscale/repack quickly because cooldown windows are long for reserved pools.
2026-03-12 19:05 - Hypothesis B: KV cache growth held memory references causing GPUs to appear 'occupied' even after stream end; garbage collection of KV entries delayed placement of new batches.

2026-03-13 09:30 - Ran controlled repro on staging with similar short-stream pattern: reproduced queue growth and elevated allocation 'no-fit' metrics. Observed that continuous-batcher refused to merge streams due to differing sequence lengths and model pinning.

2026-03-13 15:45 - Identified specific scheduler edge-case: allocator's contiguous-slot heuristic assumes slots are free in multiples of 8; many small streams left 2-3 slot fragments on GPUs leading to waste.
comments: Support (Aisha): Customer-impacting; opened incident and requested priority triage. Collected correlation IDs and SDK logs; asked CS to throttle inbound customer requests as temporary mitigation.

SRE (Marco): Looking into allocator and autoscaler logs; initial signal shows fragmentation + noisy-tenant. Spinning up placement probe and asking infra to temporarily relax contiguous-slot requirement for this pool.
Customer (LexaAI - Jenna K): We saw retries and errors during our evening campaign. Can you advise immediate actions we can take? We're considering pacing requests.

SRE (Marco): Immediate workaround: recommend customer reduce concurrent short-streams by adding jitter/pacing and enable SDK retry backoff. We've temporarily increased pool ephemeral-burst-capacity and applied a repack job (manual) to defragment slots. Please confirm whether throughput improves.
Customer (Jenna K): After pacing and you running repack, p50 improved to ~180ms and p99 dropped to ~600ms. Still seeing occasional plateaus. We'll keep paced traffic while you continue investigation.
Support (Aisha): Noted improvement; leaving ticket In Progress while engineering implements a safer autoscaler repack and a fix for KV cache cleanup.

SRE (Riley Chen): Proposed follow-up: add detection rule for 'microburst short-stream fanout' and automated repack trigger. Drafting allocator change to relax contiguous-slot heuristic when utilization > 80%.
Eng (Priya Nair): Investigating KV cache GC tuning for quick reclamation; small change PR ready for review.
resolution: Workarounds applied: immediate customer pacing plus temporary burst capacity increase and manual repack reduced impact. Engineering changes planned: (1) autoscaler: add repack-on-fragmentation threshold and reduce reserved-pool cooldown to allow faster compaction; (2) allocator: make contiguous-slot heuristic adaptive for mixed-size workloads; (3) KV cache: faster eviction/GC for ephemeral entries. Related PRs opened and in review. Postmortem planned and will include a customer communication and recommended SDK guidance for pacing short streaming bursts.
next_steps: 1) Merge autoscaler repack PR and deploy to canary by 2026-03-18.
2) Deploy KV cache GC tuning to staging and monitor reclaim latency (target < 5s) by 2026-03-16.
3) Create an automated alert for 'fractional-slot fragmentation' and add to console per-tenant dashboard.
4) Schedule postmortem with customer and internal stakeholders (runbook, timeline, and mitigation steps).
